A review of certain aggregate statistics illustrates the growth in metropolitan areas and the outward push to the suburbs over the past 3 decades. In 1940, approximately 48 percent of the Nation's population lived in urban areas (then designated "metropolitan districts" by the Bureau of Census). By 1970 this figure had grown to 70 percent. From 1950 to 1960 central city population generally increased at a rate of approximately 11 percent, while suburban fringe population grew at a rate of 48 percent. From 1960 to 1970 these figures were 6 percent and 27 percent, respectively. Finally, in 1970, 54 percent of the people in metropolitan areas resided outside the corporate boundaries of central 23 cities.
We also noted in the Interim Report the evidence submitted 24 by the Mississippi Research and Development Center, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 146. Manufacturing has replaced agriculture as the primary economic pursuit in the State, and this change has caused a population shift to urban centers.
